book.title: The Five Dysfunctions of a Team
book.author: Patrick Lencioni

confidence_note: From memory of the model section; book text not accessed. Artificial harmony, back-channel comments, ideological (idea-based) conflict, mining for conflict and real-time permission are recalled as the book's terms. No specific fable scene is included because none could be verified; the old TR text's board meeting and hallway quotes are not from the book and were dropped. 'Settles issues faster' and 'passionate and unfiltered' are paraphrases of the book's claims.
facts: The second dysfunction is fear of conflict, leading to artificial harmony.
Teams that avoid conflict have boring meetings.
Disagreements move into veiled discussions and back-channel comments.
Healthy conflict is about ideas, not personalities, and can be passionate.
Leaders should mine for conflict, pulling buried disagreements out and resisting the urge to rescue people from discomfort.
Leaders can give real-time permission mid-debate.
scene_details: the leader pulling a disagreement out of hiding
tension: A meeting everyone calls fine that settles nothing.
opening_idea: Everyone nods in the room and talks afterward.

lessons.idea: Agreement in the room can hide the debate elsewhere.

reflect_final: What opinion from your last meeting did you keep to yourself until the meeting was over?

use_cases.move: Ask for the weakest part of the plan.
Raise the concern you agreed past.

pocket_idea: Silence in a meeting means the debate is happening afterward.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A meeting with no disagreement may just move arguments elsewhere.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Artificial harmony, back-channel, mining for conflict.
